summary: Quantum oscillations of a buried InAs quantum well beneath Al, Sn, V, Nb, Ta and Re films directly measure the semiconductor's normal-state parameters—density, mass, $g$-factor, mobility and quantum lifetime—that are renormalized but not accessible to tunnelling spectroscopy. Every metal creates a distinct interface subband with occupation falling into two classes determined by orbital character rather than work function, while the buried well's mass and $g$-factor remain invariant at $0.040\text{–}0.044\,m_e$ and $|g_\mathrm{eff}| = 4.9 \pm 0.2$ across all films, and its quantum lifetime either improves or remains unchanged.
motivation: Superconductor–semiconductor hybrids require knowledge of the semiconductor's band structure, disorder and coupling strength beneath the superconductor, but the metal shunts electrical transport and blocks conventional Hall-bar characterization, forcing reliance on uncapped sister samples or spectroscopy that measure different systems.
method: Shubnikov–de Haas oscillations on unpatterned In$_{0.75}$Ga$_{0.25}$As/InAs/In$_{0.75}$Ga$_{0.25}$As heterostructure stacks resolve the buried well and interface subbands; a corrected Dingle analysis accounts for the shunt prefactor $P = (\mu_t^2 B^2 - 1)/(1 + \mu_t^2 B^2)^2$ that produces non-monotonic envelopes, and spin-zero spectroscopy in tilted fields determines $|g|m^*/m_e$ model-free.
result: Interface densities span $(5.3\text{–}6.5) \times 10^{11}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ for refractory metals and $(1.2\text{–}1.3) \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ for Al/Sn; quantum lifetimes yield upper bounds on escape rate $\Gamma_\mathrm{QW} \leq 0.18\text{–}0.6$ meV and induced-gap ceilings $\Delta_\mathrm{ind}^\mathrm{max} = 0.3\text{–}0.8\,\Delta_0$ for the buried well, constraining the quasiparticle weight $Z \geq 0.1\text{–}0.2$.
